transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-07 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Nina (CTO - Cedar Hollow), Rajiv (Sr Eng), Alice (Product)

Summary: quick initial discovery, customer evaluating Redwood for embedding search + internal AI assistant; interested in fastest path to live while keeping data in VPC long term.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, ethan is my solutions engineer, quick roundtable?
00:08 Nina: nina here CTO, quick background we run a combination of postgres + vector DB for internal knowledge, mainly embeddings today.
00:15 Rajiv: rajiv - we own infra and will be primary integrator.
00:18 Alice: alice - product owner on the assistant feature. timeline is early q2 pilot.
00:25 Maya: perfect, goal for today's call is align on time-to-first-token (ttft), what free credits look like, and whether we recommend hosted to start vs dedicated/vpc. also flag any security blockers.
00:40 Ethan: quick clarification on workload — are you planning streaming chat or short embeddings / rerank?
00:45 Nina: mostly short chat and rerank for now, maybe streaming later. latency under 250ms p50 ideal for chat, and cost is a consideration.
00:58 Rajiv: also we have strict PII controls, can't send raw customer data to third party in some flows — so vpc or onprem eventually.
01:06 Maya: makes sense — typical path is start with hosted redwood api to move fast via PLG credits, then transition to dedicated or private for data isolation. we can provide free credits to get to first token, usually 5-10k tokens is enough to demo.
01:18 Alice: can you explain what bundled support is for quickstart? we want a repeatable onboarding for PMs and devs.
01:24 Maya: yeah the quickstart playbook includes a sample repo, a prompt template, SDK snippets for node/python, and a checklist for tokenization and batching. ethan will share best-practice batching config to save on unit cost.
01:36 Ethan: one nuance — when customers move to dedicated we recommend enabling prefix caching and KV cache hot-keying. that reduces per-token compute on repeat queries, big cost saver.
01:48 Rajiv: sorry what's KV cache? i heard kv cache but sometimes transcribers write k v as k.v. cache, but yeah how intrusive is it?
01:55 Ethan: not intrusive — runtime-level optimization, you keep the key-value state for a conversation so you don't recalc attention for previous tokens. it lives in the serving layer.
02:10 Nina: on compliance, we need SOC 2 type II evidence and SSO via SAML. does redwood have those?
02:17 Maya: yes we have SOC 2 reports for hosted customers, SSO/SAML is supported, RBAC and audit logs are in the console. for private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key material.
02:30 Rajiv: KMS/HSM — do you support AWS KMS and on-prem HSM?
02:34 Maya: AWS KMS yes, GCP KMS yes, and we can plug in customer HSM for private infra — there's an onboarding process. we'll share the security docs.
02:48 Alice: how about model versions and rollouts? we need stable outputs for production.
02:54 Ethan: rollout and pinning are first-class — you can pin model ver, do canary traffic or A/B, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if capacity constrained.
03:08 Nina: okay good. question on pricing: if we start hosted then move to dedicated, how does cost transfer? do credits apply?
03:16 Maya: credits are promotional for PLG onboarding. reserved capacity has commit pricing; we can structure conversations so usage credits offset early months, but reserved contracts are separate. we'll include pricing examples in the playbook.
03:30 Rajiv: want to test throughput — our anticipated ~50 qps peak for a short window. what GPU sizing do you recommend?
03:38 Ethan: for 50 qps typical recommendation is a dedicated pool on 4xA100 equivalent with autoscale for spikes; for hosted we can accommodate with burst but with less SLA. we'll run a perf benchmark with your prompt set to validate.
03:52 Maya: noting next step — ethan will run a 1-hour benchmark using your sample prompts, include latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens and suggestions on batching/quantization.
04:03 Alice: timeline — we want a pilot in 6 weeks. is that realistic?
04:09 Maya: yes start with hosted quickstart to demo in days, then pilot with dedicated or private in 4-6 weeks depending on procurement.
04:17 Rajiv: procurement note — we have an internal security review; if hosted passes SOC 2 doc we can do a short pilot. if they flag anything, we may need private deployment later.
04:28 Nina: vendor risk team will want to see audit logs retention policy and data residency options.
04:34 Maya: we'll share the security pack and the audit log retention table. for data residency we have region-based hosting and private can be on-prem.
04:42 Rajiv: any concerns about model hallucinations for internal knowledge base?
04:46 Ethan: we recommend eval suites and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; redwood optimize will suggest quantization/profile tradeoffs but maintain quality baselines. we'll show you an eval harness in the next call.
04:58 Alice: what about latency targets, is 250ms p50 achievable on hosted?
05:03 Ethan: depending on model and sequence length, hosted can hit that for shorter prompts; dedicated gives more predictable latency SLAs. we'll validate with your real prompts.
05:15 Maya: do you have an existing vector DB provider?
05:18 Nina: we use Milvus right now, self-hosted in our VPC.
05:22 Ethan: integration is straightforward, we can show SDK pattern for retrieving vectors and calling the model for rerank.
05:30 Rajiv: any blocker for us starting the quickstart? who signs up?
05:33 Maya: you can self-serve — we'll give a credits link and the sample repo. nina or alice can create the account and invite devs.
05:40 Nina: i'll create the account and invite rajiv. small ask — can we have a short runbook for data flow so risk team understands where data travels?
05:47 Maya: yes, ethan will include a network diagram and data flow notes in the playbook.
05:54 Alice: what are typical pilot success criteria?
05:58 Ethan: we usually recommend 1) integration completed and end-to-end demo, 2) latency under target on key prompts, 3) accuracy/regression within defined thresholds on eval set, 4) a stakeholder signoff for security.
06:13 Nina: agreed. also want to measure cost per conversational session.
06:18 Maya: we'll include a cost model spreadsheet.
06:23 Rajiv: procurement Q: contract length for dedicated — any minimum?
06:27 Maya: reserved capacity typically has quarterly or annual commitments; we can show pricing bands. short pilots can run on hosted credits or a trial dedicated offer for 6-8 weeks.
06:36 Nina: one more — for private onprem, what's the order of magnitude for integration time?
06:41 Ethan: on-prem can take 6-10 weeks depending on network and compliance gating; VPC-hosted private is faster usually 3-6 weeks.
06:51 Maya: ok recap — maya will send quickstart playbook and credits, ethan will run a benchmark with your prompt set, customer to confirm compliance stakeholders. next call we'll do a technical deep dive if bench passes.
07:05 Alice: thanks all, that was very helpful.
07:10 Nina: thanks.
07:12 Maya: thanks everyone — action items noted. bye.

End of transcript.
